definition: A JavaScript game engine for creating two-dimensional games that run in a web browser.
example: A developer implements a tile-based platform game with Impact.js.

definition: A clinical breathing exercise that uses device feedback to encourage slow, deep inhalation.
example: A patient follows a clinician's guidance to use an incentive spirometer during recovery.

definition: Documenting and communicating an incident, its circumstances, and immediate responses through the appropriate reporting process.
example: A worker records a near miss so a safety team can investigate it.

definition: A web platform API for storing and querying substantial amounts of structured data locally in a browser.
example: An offline web app saves records in IndexedDB until a network connection returns.

definition: Using communication, evidence, and relationships to shape another person's understanding or decision without necessarily having formal authority.
example: A project lead gains stakeholder support by explaining the implications of several options.

definition: A database designed for ingesting, storing, and querying timestamped or time-series data.
example: An operator queries sensor measurements over a production shift.

definition: An IP address management product for tracking address space, assignments, and associated infrastructure information.
example: An administrator consults Infoblox IPAM before allocating a new subnet.

definition: Designing visual explanations that combine structured information, concise text, and graphics.
example: A communications designer turns survey results into a visual summary with labeled charts.

definition: Providing accurate information and context-sensitive support so people can understand their options and make informed choices.
example: An adviser explains course entry requirements and helps a learner compare possible pathways.
sense_note: May refer to the formal UK information, advice, and guidance service context.

definition: Assessing information for credibility, accuracy, relevance, and sufficiency for a particular purpose.
example: A researcher compares a claim against the underlying dataset and independent evidence.

definition: A software design principle that conceals implementation decisions behind stable interfaces to limit unnecessary dependencies.
example: A module exposes an operation for saving records without exposing the data format it uses internally.
sense_note: In security contexts the phrase can instead mean concealing data; the design principle is intended here.

definition: Designing or using safeguards to detect and prevent unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information.
example: A company applies approved sharing policies and reviews alerts for accidental exposure of confidential files.

definition: Examining information technology systems, controls, and processes against defined requirements or audit criteria.
example: An auditor samples account changes to check whether access reviews were completed.

definition: An industrial control platform associated with Invensys for integrating process control and plant information.
sense_note: Confirm the historical product edition and architecture before describing specific components.

definition: A relational database management system used to store and query structured data.
example: A legacy business application retrieves account records from Ingres.

definition: A MySQL storage engine that supports transactions, row-level locking, and foreign key constraints.
example: An application updates an order and its items in a single InnoDB transaction.

definition: Providing nursing care to hospitalized patients during pregnancy, labor, birth, or the postpartum period.
example: An obstetric nurse monitors a patient's condition and communicates changes to the care team.

definition: Leading sales teams that engage prospective and existing customers remotely rather than primarily through field visits.
example: A manager coaches representatives on remote demonstrations and tracks conversion rates.

definition: A vulnerability management tool used to identify, prioritize, and track remediation of security weaknesses in authorized environments.
example: A security manager reviews remediation progress for findings on company-managed assets.

definition: Planning, placing, and evaluating paid advertisements delivered through Instagram placements.
example: A marketer compares registration rates from two paid Instagram video campaigns.

definition: Producing and adapting photographs, videos, graphics, and copy for Instagram formats and audiences.
example: A creator edits a short vertical video with captions for publication.

definition: Using Instagram's content, community, analytics, and advertising features to support promotional goals.
example: A brand reviews engagement and uses the findings to plan its next posts.

definition: An Instagram feature for sharing sequences of media that are normally visible for a limited time unless preserved through supported features.
example: An event organizer posts a short sequence of behind-the-scenes updates to Stories.

definition: A social networking platform for sharing photos and videos and interacting with other accounts.
example: A museum posts photographs of its exhibits and answers visitors' comments.

definition: A commercial real-time operating system family designed for predictable execution in embedded systems.
example: An embedded engineering team evaluates the operating system for a system with strict timing requirements.

definition: A historical Intel branding program for personal computers designed to support digital home entertainment.
example: A history exhibit shows a media-center computer sold under the Intel Viiv brand.

definition: Combining automation with analytical or AI techniques to execute workflows that involve interpretation or decision support.
example: An accounts team classifies incoming documents automatically and routes uncertain cases for review.

definition: A structured course of frequent treatment sessions that allows participants to live outside a facility rather than receive inpatient care.
example: A patient attends several scheduled group and individual sessions each week while living at home.

definition: Creating or operating three-dimensional digital content that responds to user actions in real time.
example: A designer builds a model that visitors can rotate and inspect from different viewpoints.

definition: Designing how a person acts on a system or experience and how it responds.
example: A designer prototypes the feedback that follows selection of an item in a kiosk interface.

definition: Developing narratives in which a participant's actions influence how the story is revealed or what happens next.
example: A writer creates branches that change which character the player meets.

definition: Designing or producing web material that responds to user input rather than presenting fixed information alone.
example: A publisher builds an explorable graphic that updates when readers select a city.

definition: Planning the layout, controls, states, and feedback of responsive or interactive web experiences.
example: A designer specifies how filter controls alter a product grid and show active selections.

definition: Implementing interactive behavior in websites and web applications with suitable client- and server-side technologies.
example: A developer builds a filterable list that updates without reloading the full page.

definition: Coordinating work across people with different disciplinary knowledge to solve problems or produce shared outcomes.
example: A designer, clinician, and engineer jointly refine a patient-facing application.

definition: Conducting an authorized fact-finding inquiry into suspected misconduct or other issues within an organization.
example: An investigator preserves records and interviews involved staff to establish relevant facts.

definition: A standardized identifier assigned to a particular edition and format of a book or similar monographic publication.
example: A bookseller matches a hardcover edition to its ISBN.

definition: A network protocol for reporting IP delivery errors and conveying diagnostic or control messages.
example: A network administrator interprets an ICMP error indicating that a destination could not be reached.

definition: A mail access protocol for retrieving and managing messages and folders while keeping mailbox state on a server.
example: A user reads mail on a laptop and later sees the same read status on a phone.

definition: The family of layered communications protocols used to interconnect networks and support Internet applications.
example: An application sends requests over transport and IP protocols without needing to control individual network links.
